summary: Arithmetic conjugacy quotients, local-to-global torus transfer, dense Weil points and the descent of Frobenius classes for abelian varieties. The common reductive-group core of Kisin–Zhou and Kisin–Madapusi Pera–Shin is planned once. Cohomology, Mumford–Tate groups and Shimura geometry retain their existing owners; the other incoming directions have explicit split proposals.

nodes.title: Regular class functions
nodes.statement: For a commutative Hopf algebra H over a commutative ring k, define the subalgebra C(H) as the equalizer of the coordinate conjugation map c*:H→H⊗ₖH and the second-factor inclusion h↦1⊗h. For H=O(G), its elements are the regular functions invariant under conjugation on every k-algebra of points. Use the existing convolution point group and Hopf conjugation map.
hypotheses: H is commutative; the universal definition makes no reductivity or characteristic assumption.
proofSteps: Use AlgHom.equalizer. The first tensor factor of c* is the conjugator, so comparison is with the second-factor inclusion.
Evaluate the equality with productMap at arbitrary algebra-valued points. Conversely evaluate at the two universal tensor-factor points.
Use naturality of c* to restrict coordinate pullback under a group homomorphism to these subalgebras.
acceptance: Invariance is pointwise equality, stronger than stability of a subring under conjugation.

sources.match: The affine group conjugacy quotient uses the conjugation-invariant coordinate algebra; the equalizer gives its universal coordinate meaning.

nodes.title: Highest-weight characters and orbit sums
nodes.statement: For a connected split reductive group G over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, with B⊃T and the associated positive roots, each dominant character λ∈X*(T) is the highest weight of a unique simple rational G-representation V(λ). Its highest weight space has dimension one and all other weights are λ minus a nonzero sum of positive simple roots. Its character is W-invariant. Consequently the irreducible characters form a k-basis of k[X*(T)]^W, by unitriangular comparison with Weyl orbit sums. The full character lattice, including central directions, is retained.
hypotheses: Use dominant characters in X*(T), not all dominant weights of the simply connected covering group.
The lattice/central-isogeny descent condition is part of the statement.
proofSteps: For existence, import Tau Ceti’s current Hopf-ideal line-stabilizer theorem through the requested Layer 1 dictionary and apply it to a parabolic subgroup to obtain positive multiples of fundamental weights. On the big Bruhat cell construct the B-equivariant regular function of a desired dominant weight; a positive power extends globally, and normality of G makes the original function extend.

The regular representation is locally finite. Its generated highest-weight module has one-dimensional highest weight and a unique simple quotient. The root subgroup expansion proves all remaining weights lie below the highest weight; the direct-sum highest-vector argument proves uniqueness.

Pass from a semisimple group times a torus through the central isogeny: a representation descends precisely when its highest character lies in X*(T). Normalizer representatives permute weight spaces, giving W-invariance.

Subtract leading orbit sums, within each central-character coset; the dominance intervals involved are finite. This proves the triangular character basis needed for restriction, without planning modular representations or the Lie-algebra Weyl character formula again.
acceptance: For PGL₂ only even SL₂ highest weights occur. For G_m all integers occur and the character basis is the Laurent monomial basis.

Over ℂ for GL_n, SL_n, SO_n and Sp_n, identify this classification with ClassicalGroups Layer 3 by the unique simple highest-weight representation; do not reconstruct its classical carriers or Schur functors. The new theorem is the rational algebraic-group statement for arbitrary connected reductive G, not a second Lie-module classification.

sources.match: Gives and proves the rational group highest-weight classification and central-isogeny descent.
Uses highest weights and orbit-sum triangularity for the character basis.

nodes.title: Group Chevalley restriction
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive G over k of characteristic zero and a maximal k-torus T with Weyl group scheme W=N_G(T)/T, restriction is C(O(G))≅O(T)^W; thus Conj(G)≅T/W as affine schemes. Over an algebraic closure Ω, χ_G gives a bijection between geometric semisimple G(Ω)-conjugacy classes and Conj(G)(Ω).
hypotheses: The quotient is for group elements, not the Lie algebra adjoint quotient.
A maximal k-torus exists; W acts on T by conjugation.
proofSteps: Over an algebraically closed field, every semisimple element lies in a maximal torus, all maximal tori are conjugate, and intersection of a semisimple class with T is one Weyl orbit.

Extend Steinberg’s highest-weight triangular argument to the full character lattice of a reductive group: irreducible characters span the Weyl-invariant group algebra, including the central character coordinates. Do not infer polynomiality from the simply connected semisimple case.

Restrict to regular semisimple elements for injectivity; descend the restriction isomorphism and the finite Weyl quotient along field extension. Finite-group invariant algebra proves finite generation.
acceptance: For G_m the quotient retains the whole torus. The general reductive quotient need not be affine space.

sources.match: Proves the character and restriction statements for semisimple groups; the stated reductive extension uses the same highest-weight argument with central characters.
Uses the maximal-torus quotient and the geometric semisimple-class description.

nodes.title: The affine conjugacy quotient
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive group G over a characteristic-zero field k, construct Conj(G)=Spec C(O(G)) and χ_G:G→Conj(G) from the subalgebra inclusion. It is the categorical quotient for conjugation among affine k-schemes: invariant maps G→Y factor uniquely through χ_G. The coordinate algebra is finitely generated. Formation commutes with extension of fields, and group homomorphisms induce quotient maps.
hypotheses: G is smooth affine, geometrically connected and reductive; char k=0.
proofSteps: Construct Spec and its map contravariantly from the inclusion. The affine universal property follows from the equalizer.
Establish finite generation and field base change using the torus–Weyl comparison below; prove that comparison first on coordinate algebras, without relying on a pre-existing quotient.
An invariant morphism is tested as an equality on G×G, not only on k-rational points.
acceptance: The universal property is among affine schemes; no claim that this is the set of rational conjugacy classes.

sources.match: Defines Conj(G) as an affine quotient, with χ_G and its geometric semisimple-class interpretation.
Restriction identifies the semisimple-group invariant coordinate algebra with torus Weyl invariants; the reductive extension is an explicit target here.

nodes.title: Characters separate semisimple classes
nodes.statement: For semisimple x,y∈G(Ω), where Ω is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, the following are equivalent: x and y are G(Ω)-conjugate; χ_G(x)=χ_G(y); every finite-dimensional algebraic representation has the same trace at x and y; every such representation has the same characteristic polynomial at x and y.
hypotheses: G is connected reductive; both elements are semisimple.
proofSteps: Use group Chevalley restriction and the highest-weight spanning of invariant regular functions by characters.
Characteristic polynomials imply traces; equality of all traces gives equality of quotient points. Conjugacy implies equality of every characteristic polynomial.
acceptance: One faithful representation alone need not separate classes: t↦diag(t,t⁻¹) identifies 2 and 1/2 in G_m.

sources.match: For semisimple groups equates conjugacy with equality of characters and representation classes; the reductive extension is supplied by group restriction.
Applies all-representation character data to compare Frobenius quotient points.

nodes.title: Finite faithful representation quotient
nodes.statement: If ρ:G↪GL(V) is a closed faithful algebraic representation of a connected reductive group over a characteristic-zero field, the induced morphism Conj(G)→Conj(GL(V)) is finite. It is not asserted injective.
hypotheses: Faithfulness means a closed immersion of algebraic groups, not injectivity on rational points.
V is finite-dimensional.
proofSteps: Base change to an algebraic closure and choose a maximal torus T. Its representation weights generate X*(T), since the torus representation is a closed immersion.

Every weight value is integral over the characteristic-polynomial coefficients. Its inverse is integral after adjoining the inverse determinant, by the reciprocal characteristic polynomial. Hence O(T) is finite over the image coefficient algebra.
The Weyl invariants are a submodule of this finite module over a noetherian coefficient image, hence finite. Descend finiteness to k.
acceptance: For G_m↪GL₂ via t↦diag(t,t⁻¹), the map is finite of generic degree two, illustrating why finite is the required conclusion.

sources.match: Uses the finite map induced by a faithful representation to obtain algebraicity of quotient points.

nodes.title: Orthogonal outer automorphisms
nodes.statement: For connected reductive H over a characteristic-zero field F, write H_der over F̄ as an almost direct product of its actual almost simple normal factors H_i. Select those isomorphic to SO(2n_i), n_i≥4. The product of O(2n_i)/SO(2n_i) over these factors descends, with the Galois permutation action, to a finite étale group Out′(H). Construct its canonical action on Conj(H), set Conj′(H)=Conj(H)/Out′(H), and define Aut′(H) as its inverse image in Aut(H)→Out(H).
hypotheses: Select actual SO factors, not every factor with a Dynkin diagram of type D.
The order-two orthogonal action in type D₄ does not include triality.
proofSteps: An improper orthogonal conjugation acts on its SO factor, fixes its scalar centre, and hence extends through the almost direct product with the other factors and connected centre.
Changing an orthogonal realization changes the action only by inner conjugation, which acts trivially on Conj(H). The factor set and these actions are Galois stable, giving descent.
Take the finite affine quotient of the invariant algebra; establish base change and the relationship between Aut′-orbits and Conj′ points.
acceptance: When the index set is empty Out′ is trivial and Conj′=Conj. Do not replace the definition by all diagram automorphisms.

sources.match: Specifies the actual SO factors, their orthogonal outer quotients and Aut′; refers to Noot §1.5 for the construction.

nodes.title: Jordan’s conjugacy covering lemma
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a finite group and Δ≤Γ. If every element of Γ is conjugate to an element of Δ, then Δ=Γ. Equivalently every proper subgroup misses a conjugacy class.
hypotheses: No normality of Δ is assumed.
proofSteps: Act transitively on Γ/Δ. A conjugate of g belongs to Δ exactly when g fixes a coset.

Burnside’s formula makes the average number of fixed cosets one. If every element fixes a coset and [Γ:Δ]>1, the identity contributes more than one and every other element at least one, contradicting that average.
acceptance: For Γ=S₃ a point stabilizer misses the class of 3-cycles.

sources.match: The residue-field descent invokes Jordan’s finite-group lemma.

nodes.title: Rational descent from local realizations
nodes.statement: Let X be an affine finite-type ℚ-scheme and a∈X(ℚ̄). If, for all but finitely many rational primes ℓ, the geometric point obtained using a specified embedding ℚ̄↪ℚ̄_ℓ belongs to X(ℚ_ℓ), then a∈X(ℚ). The embeddings may vary with ℓ.
hypotheses: The point is algebraic and the same ℚ̄-point is compared at every prime.
proofSteps: Let F be the residue field of the image closed point of a. Its realization in ℚ_ℓ gives a degree-one place of F over each allowed ℓ, after removing the finitely many ramified primes.
In a Galois closure L/ℚ with Γ=Gal(L/ℚ) and Δ=Gal(L/F), degree-one splitting means Frobenius fixes a coset of Δ, equivalently its class meets Δ.
Chebotarev and the finite exceptional set imply every conjugacy class meets Δ. Jordan gives Δ=Γ and F=ℚ.
acceptance: Having a degree-one prime is weaker than complete splitting; the proof does not make that invalid substitution.

sources.match: Descends a common algebraic quotient point using degree-one primes, Chebotarev and Jordan.

nodes.title: Algebraicity above rational invariants
nodes.statement: For a finite morphism f:X→Y of affine finite-type ℚ-schemes, y∈Y(ℚ), and x∈X(ℚ_ℓ) above y, the residue field of x is finite over ℚ. After choosing an embedding of that residue field in ℚ̄ and then into ℚ̄_ℓ compatible with x, x is the realization of an algebraic point. In particular a Frobenius quotient point with rational characteristic polynomial is algebraic.
hypotheses: Finiteness, rather than mere finite type, is essential.
proofSteps: The fibre has finite-dimensional coordinate algebra over ℚ. A map to ℚ_ℓ factors through a finite field quotient.
Apply the faithful quotient finiteness theorem to the rational characteristic-polynomial point. Equality of these algebraic points across primes is a separate input.
acceptance: For A¹→Spec ℚ, an arbitrary ℓ-adic coordinate need not be algebraic over ℚ; finite type is insufficient.

sources.match: The finite faithful quotient map first establishes algebraicity, before the common-point rationality argument.

nodes.title: Conjugacy quotients of inner forms
nodes.statement: An inner twisting ψ:G_ℚ̄≅G′_ℚ̄ induces a ℚ-isomorphism Conj(G)≅Conj(G′). It depends only on the inner-twisting class: changing ψ by an inner automorphism has no effect. The isomorphism carries geometric semisimple classes and commutes with extension of scalars. The same assertion holds over any characteristic-zero field.
hypotheses: The twist must be inner; a general outer twist can act nontrivially on the quotient.
proofSteps: The discrepancy between σψ and ψ is inner and therefore acts trivially on regular class functions. Apply affine Galois descent to their coordinate algebra map.
Identity, inverse and composition laws follow from the corresponding maps before descent and invariance under inner conjugation.
acceptance: This comparison identifies quotient points, not rational representatives or rational conjugacy classes.

sources.match: An embedding change gives an inner twist and hence a canonical comparison of the conjugacy quotients.

nodes.title: Diagonal restriction-of-scalars injection
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ be a finite extension, G connected reductive, and H⊂Res_{F/ℚ}G_F a connected reductive ℚ-subgroup containing the diagonal copy of G. The induced map Conj(G)(ℚ̄)→Conj(H)(ℚ̄) is injective and Γ_ℚ-equivariant. In particular this applies to the common-multiplier fibre product H=(Res G_F)×_{Res G_m}G_m for a character ν:G→G_m.
hypotheses: The inclusion into the Weil restriction is the stated diagonal embedding.
proofSteps: Over ℚ̄ the Weil restriction is a product of copies of G. If two diagonal semisimple points are H-conjugate, any component of a conjugator conjugates the original points in G.
Use the geometric quotient description and the fact that all maps are defined over ℚ.
acceptance: The proof asserts injectivity on geometric quotient points; it does not replace it by injectivity on G(ℚ).

sources.match: The common-multiplier auxiliary group embeds in the Weil restriction and preserves geometric conjugacy classes of the diagonal group.

nodes.title: Central-product quotient injection
nodes.statement: Let H be connected reductive over a characteristic-zero field and T a torus containing Z_H as a closed subgroup. For H₁=(H×T)/{(z,z⁻¹):z∈Z_H}, the embedding h↦[(h,1)] induces an injection Conj(H)(Ω)→Conj(H₁)(Ω) for algebraically closed Ω, equivariant for descent to the base field.
hypotheses: T is commutative and the two centre embeddings use the displayed inverse.
proofSteps: Lift an H₁(Ω)-conjugator to (h,t) using surjectivity on algebraically closed points of the central quotient.
Its conjugation on [(x,1)] is [(hxh⁻¹,1)]. Equality with [(y,1)] forces the antidiagonal central element to have torus coordinate 1, hence to be 1; therefore hxh⁻¹=y.
acceptance: The torus coordinate is indispensable: quotienting H by its centre alone need not preserve distinct semisimple classes.

sources.match: The commutative torus factor of the central product introduces no new geometric conjugacies.

nodes.title: Global torus classes with prescribed real value
nodes.statement: For every ℚ-torus T and rational prime p, the localization map ker[H¹(ℚ,T)→H¹(ℚ_p,T)]→H¹(ℝ,T) is surjective. More precisely, a prescribed real class can be realized by a global class trivial at p and at every finite place except one auxiliary ℓ≠p, chosen in a positive-density Chebotarev set outside any specified finite set.
hypotheses: Use ordinary Galois H¹ of a torus and the Tate–Nakayama normalization imported from ET.0.
proofSteps: Choose a finite Galois splitting field and a complex-conjugation element c. At an unramified auxiliary ℓ with Frobenius conjugate to c, local coinvariant torsion maps to the same global coinvariant group as the real localization.
Choose its local class to cancel the prescribed real image. The torus local-to-global exact sequence lifts the tuple to H¹(ℚ,T). The p-component was set to zero.
Chebotarev supplies infinitely many admissible ℓ and permits avoiding a finite set. If the real cohomology is zero the trivial class suffices.
acceptance: For T=G_m every group H¹ here is zero. For the imaginary quadratic norm-one torus the nontrivial real class requires the auxiliary finite component.

sources.match: Constructs a global torus class with specified real value and trivial p-component.
Identifies the global obstruction and exactness of the adelic localization sequence needed for the construction.

nodes.title: Approximation of maximal tori
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over a number field F, S a finite set of places, and T_v⊂G_{F_v} maximal tori. There exists a maximal F-torus T⊂G such that T_{F_v} is G(F_v)-conjugate to T_v for every v∈S.
hypotheses: S may include real places and a designated finite place.
This is approximation of torus conjugacy types, not weak approximation for G(F).
proofSteps: Choose regular semisimple Lie elements whose connected centralizers are the prescribed tori. Local regular-semisimple conjugacy and the local inverse function theorem make each required centralizer type an open condition in Lie(G)(F_v).

Apply weak approximation to the F-vector space Lie(G); its chosen global point is regular semisimple because that condition holds at a place. Its centralizer is a maximal F-torus with the required local conjugacies.
acceptance: Taking S={p,∞} combines a prescribed p-adic torus with an elliptic real one. No approximation of a prescribed element of G(F_v) by G(F) is assumed.

sources.match: States simultaneous approximation of maximal tori, including archimedean places.
Restates Harder’s maximal-torus approximation result with finite place set.

nodes.title: Global tori with elliptic real fibre
nodes.statement: If G/ℚ has an elliptic maximal torus over ℝ and T_p⊂G_ℚp is any maximal torus, there is a maximal ℚ-torus T whose real fibre is elliptic and whose p-fibre is G(ℚ_p)-conjugate to T_p. Here elliptic means anisotropic modulo Z_G.
hypotheses: Existence of an elliptic real maximal torus is a hypothesis, supplied for the relevant Shimura groups by their Cartan-involution theory.
proofSteps: Apply maximal-torus approximation to {∞,p}. Ellipticity is preserved by real conjugation.
For a basic Newton application use the existing BG1 elliptic-torus image theorem; do not define B(G) or basic classes again.
acceptance: For split GL₂ one may prescribe the imaginary quadratic real torus and any chosen quadratic or split torus at p.

sources.match: Uses a global maximal torus with elliptic real fibre and the prescribed local Newton-torus behaviour.

nodes.title: Real Weyl cocycles
nodes.statement: For G/ℚ reductive, a maximal ℚ-torus T with T_sc=(preimage of T in G_sc) anisotropic over ℝ, and a representative n∈N_{G_sc}(T_sc)(ℂ) of a real Galois-invariant Weyl element w, define a=n⁻¹c(n)∈T_sc(ℂ). It is a real 1-cocycle and its class is independent of n. Complex conjugation acts by −1 on X_*(T_sc), so every Weyl element is real Galois invariant.
hypotheses: The formula is n⁻¹c(n) throughout; changing to c(n) n⁻¹ requires changing the twisting convention.
Representatives are chosen over ℂ; membership in T follows from Galois invariance of w.
proofSteps: Calculate ac(a)=1 and show a∈T_sc because n and c(n) have the same Weyl image.
Replacing n by nt changes a by t⁻¹ac(t), hence by a coboundary. Anisotropy of the real torus gives c=−1 on its cocharacter lattice, which commutes with every Weyl element.
acceptance: The cocycle represents the boundary of w for the normalizer extension; it is not generally the trivial torus class.

sources.match: Uses the torus cocycle attached to a Weyl representative to alter the real cocharacter without changing the p-local type.

nodes.title: Global adjustment of real cocharacters
nodes.statement: Let G/ℚ be connected reductive, T a maximal ℚ-torus with T_sc anisotropic over ℝ, h:S→T_ℝ a real Hodge homomorphism and μ_h its complex Hodge cocharacter. Given μ∈X_*(T_ℚ̄) and w∈W(G,T)(ℂ) with wμ=μ_h, there exist g∈G_sc(ℚ̄), a maximal ℚ-torus T′=gTg⁻¹ and h′ in the G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of h factoring through T′_ℝ, such that μ_{h′}=gμg⁻¹. Moreover T′_ℚp is G_sc(ℚ_p)-conjugate to T_ℚp, and this identification transports μ to μ_{h′} up to T-conjugacy.
hypotheses: Fix embeddings ℚ̄→ℂ and ℚ̄→ℚ̄_p and use the induced interpretation of μ.
Choose n representing w and the cocycle a=n⁻¹ c(n). Its image in H¹(ℝ,G_sc) is trivial because it is a coboundary there.
proofSteps: Lift [a] to H¹(ℚ,T_sc) with zero p-component by the auxiliary-place theorem. Its image in H¹(ℚ,G_sc) is trivial at infinity, hence globally trivial by the simply connected Hasse theorem. Represent it by g⁻¹σ(g); then gTg⁻¹ descends to ℚ.
At infinity, write g⁻¹c(g)=t⁻¹n⁻¹c(n)c(t). Then u=gt⁻¹n⁻¹ is real, and Int(g)(μ)=Int(u)(wμ)=Int(u)(μ_h). Set h′=Int(u)h.
The zero p-component gives a local trivializer t_p with g t_p⁻¹∈G_sc(ℚ_p). This element conjugates T_ℚp to T′_ℚp and has the same action as g on its cocharacters, since t_p centralizes T.
acceptance: With the identity Weyl element use the trivial cocycle and g=1. Local conjugacy at p is retained, not an equality of chosen embeddings.

sources.match: Adjusts a global maximal torus and its cocharacter using a real Weyl cocycle, while preserving local conjugacy at p.

nodes.title: The Serre condition for tori
nodes.statement: A ℚ-torus T satisfies the Serre condition when its maximal ℝ-split subtorus T_s⊂T_ℝ is the base change of a ℚ-split subtorus of T. Equivalently, for a finite Galois splitting field and a complex conjugation c, the +1 eigenspace of c on X_*(T)⊗ℚ is the Γ_ℚ-fixed subspace. This is descent of the actual maximal real split torus, not merely equality of numerical ranks.
hypotheses: T is a torus over ℚ; an embedding ℚ̄↪ℂ is fixed.
proofSteps: Use the existing character/cocharacter description of tori. The maximal real split subtorus has the saturated cocharacter lattice in the +1 eigenspace.
The eigenspace equality makes the Γ action trivial on that lattice and hence descends it as a split subtorus. The converse follows by descent.

The −1 eigenspace is Galois invariant under this condition: c acts as +1 on the trivial summand and −1 on its complement in the semisimple rational Γ-module. This descends the maximal compact real subtorus T_c to ℚ, with T/T_c ℚ-split.
acceptance: A rank comparison without descent data is not a replacement for the condition.

sources.match: The Serre condition descends the real split and compact parts so characters have controlled absolute values.

nodes.title: Prime-units in algebraic groups
nodes.statement: For a number field F, a linear algebraic group H/F, a rational prime l and γ∈H(F), say γ is an l-unit when for every finite place v of F not dividing l, the cyclic subgroup {γⁿ:n∈ℤ} is bounded in H(F_v). Boundedness is the existing local algebraic-group notion, equivalently relatively compact in the local point topology. No condition is imposed at archimedean places.
hypotheses: Use all integer powers, not only positive powers.
A faithful closed algebraic embedding into GL_n can be used to test boundedness.
proofSteps: Transfer boundedness through closed algebraic embeddings using the local topology supplier.
For a semisimple torus point, diagonalize over a splitting field: boundedness of all positive and negative powers is equivalent to valuation zero for every eigencharacter.
Show functoriality under group morphisms, conjugacy invariance, and closure under multiplication for commuting points. Do not assert that all l-units of a noncommutative H form a subgroup.
acceptance: The topology at real places plays no role in this definition.

sources.match: Defines the prime-unit condition using bounded cyclic subgroups away from the distinguished prime.

api.name: PrimeUnit.iff_characters
api.statement: For a torus, γ is an l-unit iff every geometric character value has valuation zero at all finite places away from l.

api.name: PrimeUnit.map

api.name: PrimeUnit.zpow

api.name: PrimeUnit.conj

uses.how: Converts local valuation conditions to Weil eigenvalues.
The torus subgroup of prime-units is produced by adelic class finiteness.

The full cyclic subgroup is unbounded as well. Thus boundedness of entries in the ambient affine line is not the group boundedness used for l-units.

nodes.title: Prime-Weil numbers
nodes.statement: For a rational prime l and integer w, an l-Weil number of weight w is α∈ℚ̄× such that α is a unit at every finite place away from l and |σ(α)|=l^(w/2) for every embedding σ:ℚ(α)↪ℂ. We allow negative weights and do not require α to be an algebraic integer at l.
hypotheses: A nonzero algebraic number, the prime l and the integer weight are part of the data.
proofSteps: Express the finite-place condition on the number field ℚ(α); it is invariant under enlarging that field.
Absolute values under all embeddings make the condition Galois invariant. Multiplication adds weights and inversion negates weights.
acceptance: An l-Weil number has a unique weight for fixed l. Roots of unity have weight zero.

sources.match: Defines l-Weil numbers with prime-unit and all-complex-embedding absolute-value conditions.

nodes.title: Weil points of algebraic groups
nodes.statement: For a linear algebraic group H/ℚ and rational prime l, γ∈H(ℚ) is an l-Weil point when, in one faithful finite-dimensional algebraic representation, all eigenvalues of γ are l-Weil numbers, allowing different eigenvalues to have different integral weights. A Weil point is an l-Weil point for some l. Eigenvalues are compared in algebraic closures using the algebraic action of the rational point.
hypotheses: The representation is a closed algebraic immersion.
Semisimplicity is not included; neat semisimple points impose it separately.
proofSteps: Every algebraic representation is a subquotient of a finite direct sum of tensor products of the faithful representation and its dual.
Tensor products multiply eigenvalues, duals invert them, and subquotients select eigenvalues. Apply the corresponding Weil-number closure rules.
This proves independence of the faithful representation and preservation under algebraic group morphisms, even when the point has a unipotent part.
acceptance: Different weights are permitted; a common weight requires an extra scalar/polarization argument in the geometric application.

sources.match: Defines Weil points and proves representation independence by tensor generation.

A dense subgroup of neat Weil points rigidifies a family of embeddings.

nodes.title: Neatness and cyclic torus closures
nodes.statement: For a semisimple point γ∈H(F), F a number field with a fixed embedding in ℂ, the Zariski closure S of the cyclic subgroup generated by γ is diagonalizable. It is connected, hence a torus, exactly when the eigenvalues in a faithful F-representation generate a torsion-free subgroup of ℂ×. Thus neatness in the sense of KMPS is semisimplicity together with the existing adelic-groups notion of neatness. For a fixed ℚ-torus split by L, raising every rational point to n=#μ(L) makes its cyclic closure connected.
hypotheses: The torus assertion requires semisimplicity.
F-neatness is not neatness after restriction of scalars to ℚ; compare spectra with the same coefficient embedding.
proofSteps: Embed S in a split diagonal torus after scalar extension. Its character group is the quotient of a free lattice by the characters evaluating to 1 at γ. Torsion in that quotient corresponds exactly to roots of unity in the generated eigenvalue group.
For γ∈T(ℚ) and T split by L, all character values belong to L×. Torsion is killed by #μ(L); the cyclic closure of γⁿ is therefore connected.
Import the existing representation-independence theorem for neatness; do not introduce a second eigenvalue-neat predicate.
acceptance: 1 is neat; −1 is not. diag(2,4) has connected one-dimensional cyclic closure inside a two-dimensional torus. A nontrivial unipotent has connected closure G_a but not a torus.

sources.match: Uses connected cyclic closure for semisimple neat points and a uniform power to obtain them.

nodes.title: Weil points from the Serre condition
nodes.statement: For a ℚ-torus T satisfying the Serre condition and a rational prime l, γ∈T(ℚ) is an l-Weil point iff it is an l-unit. Consequently the l-Weil points form a subgroup. The same equivalence holds for semisimple rational points in a connected reductive ℚ-group all of whose maximal tori satisfy the Serre condition.
hypotheses: No group closure assertion is made for arbitrary noncommuting points of a reductive group.
proofSteps: A Weil point has unit eigencharacters away from l, hence bounded cyclic subgroup at those places.

Conversely let T_c be the descended compact subtorus. For any character χ, χ+cχ factors through the split quotient and is rational. Its value at γ is positive and is a rational l-unit, hence l^w for an integer w.
The rationality of χ+cχ makes this value the same under every embedding of the character-value field. Thus |σχ(γ)|=l^(w/2) for all σ, proving the Weil condition.
acceptance: The real-quadratic norm-one torus shows the Serre hypothesis matters: 2+√3 is a prime-unit at every finite place but its two real absolute values differ.

sources.match: Character norms convert prime-unit conditions into Weil absolute values for Serre tori.

nodes.title: Density of neat Weil points
nodes.statement: If a ℚ-torus T satisfies the Serre condition and is split over ℚ_l, then T(ℚ) contains a Zariski-dense subgroup consisting of neat l-Weil points. One can take the n-th powers of its l-Weil subgroup, for n=#μ(L) with L a finite Galois splitting field.
hypotheses: The distinguished prime l splits T; the finite adelic torus class number is imported.
proofSteps: By the unit criterion the l-Weil points form the torus subgroup of l-units. Suppose its Zariski closure is proper; a nonzero character of the quotient over ℚ_l detects a missing torus direction.

Choose an l-adic torus point on which that character has nonzero valuation. In the finite adelic class group modulo a compact open subgroup, some power of its idele is represented by a rational point times that compact open.
The rational point is a unit away from l and has nonzero detected valuation at l, contradicting triviality of the character on the closure.
Taking n-th powers preserves Zariski density because the power map of a torus is an isogeny; the cyclic-closure comparison makes all these points neat.
acceptance: For G_m, {l^(nm):m∈ℤ} is already a dense subgroup of neat l-Weil points. The statement does not say every individual point generates a dense subgroup of T.

sources.match: Uses finite adelic class number and a split distinguished prime to prove density, then a uniform power to obtain neat points.

nodes.title: Rigidity under a finite automorphism group
nodes.statement: Let S be a reduced irreducible separated finite-type scheme over k, Γ⊂S(k) a Zariski-dense subset, W≤Aut_k(S) finite, and σ∈Aut_k(S). If for each γ∈Γ there exists w∈W with σ(γ)=w(γ), then σ=w for a single w∈W.
hypotheses: S is reduced, irreducible, separated and of finite type; Γ is dense in the underlying Zariski space.
proofSteps: For each w, the equalizer of σ and w is closed because S is separated. Their finite union contains Γ, so irreducibility forces one equalizer to have the entire underlying space.
The corresponding closed subscheme is all S because S is reduced; hence the morphisms are equal. This applies to algebraic tori.
acceptance: On Spec k[ε]/(ε²) in characteristic zero, ε↦2ε fixes the only rational point but is not the identity. On the affine line with doubled origin, swapping the origins fixes the dense common punctured line.

sources.match: The finite dense-set argument is valid for reduced separated schemes; the hypotheses stated here repair its scheme-level omission.

nodes.title: Conjugacy of common-source realizations
nodes.statement: Let I,G be connected reductive ℚ-groups, Ω an algebraically closed characteristic-zero overfield with specified embeddings of all coefficient fields, and i_a:I_Ω→G_Ω a family of closed embeddings. Assume there is a central semisimple δ∈I(ℚ) such that i_a identifies I_Ω with Z_G(i_a(δ))°; all i_a(δ) lie in one Aut′(G)(Ω)-orbit. Assume a maximal ℚ-torus T⊂I has a Zariski-dense subset Γ⊂T(ℚ) such that, for each γ∈Γ, all i_a(γ) have the same Conj′(G) point. Then all i_a are conjugate by Aut′(G)(Ω). If Out′(G)=1 they are inner conjugate.
hypotheses: The common overfield and embeddings are data; unrelated local fields are not silently identified.
The centralizer-isomorphism hypotheses are essential, beyond equality of individual characteristic polynomials.
proofSteps: A connected semisimple centralizer has the same rank as G, so the images of T are maximal tori of G as well. Use Aut′ to make the images of δ agree, and conjugate the maximal tori of its connected centralizer to align all i_a(T). This uses only conjugacy of maximal tori in a connected reductive centralizer, not that the centralizer is a Levi subgroup.

For two aligned maps their ratio is an automorphism of I₀=Z_G(i_a(δ))°. On the aligned maximal torus, each point of the dense subset differs by an element of the finite automorphism group induced by the Aut′ normalizer.

Apply finite-orbit rigidity to obtain one normalizer automorphism agreeing on the torus. It fixes δ and hence preserves I₀. The difference from the original automorphism fixes the torus pointwise, so it is conjugation by an element of that torus.
acceptance: No-type-D is a sufficient condition for Out′=1 in the application, but the theorem uses the exact Out′ rather than all diagram automorphisms.

sources.match: The comparison proof is isolated here with its exact centralizer and dense-point inputs; no geometric realization theorem is assumed implicitly.

nodes.title: Galois invariance from local embedding classes
nodes.statement: Let Γ_F act continuously on a finite set X and x∈X. If, for almost all finite places v, the orbit Γ_F·x contains a point fixed by a decomposition group at v, then x is Γ_F-fixed. Apply this to the finite orbit of a geometric conjugacy class of embeddings T_ℚ̄→G_ℚ̄, whose representative is defined over a finite extension.
hypotheses: The orbit is finite; a chosen embedding morphism is of finite presentation and hence defined over a number field.
Local existence supplies a fixed point in the same orbit, not necessarily the initially selected point.
proofSteps: Pass to the finite Galois quotient acting on the orbit. Every allowed Frobenius fixes a point, hence its conjugacy class meets the stabilizer of x.
Chebotarev and Jordan force that stabilizer to be the whole quotient.
acceptance: This proves invariance of a class. Choosing a rational representative is a distinct quasi-split embedding theorem.

sources.match: Promotes the locally defined common embedding class to a global Galois-invariant geometric class.

nodes.title: Rational embeddings in quasi-split groups
nodes.statement: Let T be a ℚ-torus and G*/ℚ a quasi-split connected reductive group. Suppose a finite Galois orbit of geometric conjugacy classes of maximal-torus embeddings T_ℚ̄↪G*_ℚ̄ has the following property: at almost every finite place, a decomposition group fixes some class in that orbit. Then that orbit is a singleton and its class has a representative defined over ℚ. In particular, a common geometric maximal-torus embedding class with a local representative at every ℚ_l admits a rational representative. The general quasi-split embedding theorem is imported from ET.0; this target is its arithmetic descent application.
hypotheses: The embeddings identify T with a maximal torus, not an arbitrary subtorus.
The conclusion is the rationality of a maximal-torus embedding, not just of an element in the affine quotient.
proofSteps: Use Galois-class descent for the locally defined common class.
Apply the quasi-split maximal-torus embedding theorem, Kottwitz 1982 Corollary 2.2, through the exact ET.0 supplier contract.
acceptance: A rational Conj(G*) point is not itself a rational embedding of a prescribed torus.

sources.match: Invokes Kottwitz 1982, Corollary 2.2, to realize the invariant maximal-torus embedding class in the quasi-split inner form.

nodes.title: Local-to-global transfer of maximal tori
nodes.statement: Let G*/ℚ be quasi-split and ψ:G*_ℚ̄→G_ℚ̄ an inner twist. Let T*⊂G* be a maximal ℚ-torus whose geometric embedding transfers to G over every completion ℚ_v. If its image in G*_ad is anisotropic at at least one place, then the embedding transfers globally: there exists a maximal ℚ-torus T⊂G and a ℚ-isomorphism T*≅T geometrically conjugate to ψ|T*.
hypotheses: Transfer means an isomorphism of embedded tori induced by an inner twist after geometric conjugation; use ET.0’s definition.
The simply connected Hasse theorem is used in its modern form without an E₈ exclusion.
proofSteps: Use the torus-embedding obstruction theorem cited in LR87 Lemma 5.6: the obstruction lies in global Tate cohomology Ĥ⁻¹(Γ,X_*(T*_sc)) modulo the images of the local groups, with its natural localization maps.
At a place where T*_ad is anisotropic, the relevant norm-invariant lattice vanishes; the local-to-global map on that Tate cohomology is surjective. Thus the obstruction quotient vanishes.
Use the simply connected Hasse principle to pass from the vanishing obstruction to a global inner conjugation of the torus embedding.
acceptance: Local transfer at almost all places is insufficient for this statement: every place is required.

sources.match: Proves global transfer from local transfer and anisotropy at one place, using Langlands Lemma 7.15 for the obstruction.
Applies this theorem with ellipticity at the real place.

nodes.title: Rational tori for common realizations
nodes.statement: In the common-source situation, suppose all maximal ℚ-tori of I satisfy the Serre condition, δ is a central neat Weil point, and every neat Weil point of I(ℚ) has a rational Conj′(G) image independent of the realization. Assume G_ad has no type-D factor and G_ℚp is quasi-split. The realization embeddings provide local transfer at every finite l≠p. At infinity assume there is a real embedding i_∞:I_ℝ→G_ℝ in their common geometric class, with i_∞(I_ℝ)/(i_∞(I_ℝ)∩Z_G) anisotropic, so its real points are compact. Then every maximal ℚ-torus T⊂I admits a ℚ-embedding into G geometrically conjugate to every i_a|T.
hypotheses: Retain all centralizer-isomorphism and common-overfield hypotheses of common-source conjugacy.
The real compactness modulo the ambient centre ensures the image of every T in G_ad is anisotropic. A compact Cartan alone would not ensure this.
At p quasi-splitness supplies local transfer; the stipulated real embedding supplies it at infinity.
proofSteps: Choose a prime l splitting T. Density gives the required dense neat Weil subgroup; common-source conjugacy makes all restricted maps geometrically conjugate.
Descend their conjugacy class by Galois-class descent, realize it rationally in the quasi-split inner form, and check local transfer at every place.

Apply global torus transfer: the real embedding gives the required anisotropic image at infinity for this T. The resulting rational embedding is geometrically, not necessarily locally rationally, conjugate to the finite realization maps.
acceptance: This conclusion does not assert G(ℚ_l)-conjugacy for every l.

sources.match: Separates the reductive descent argument from the preceding geometric theorem for isogeny-group realizations.

nodes.title: Odd unitary similitude Hasse principle
nodes.statement: Let F/F⁺ be any CM quadratic extension, with F⁺ totally real of odd degree over ℚ. Let G be the unitary similitude ℚ-group of an odd-dimensional hermitian F-space with one common rational multiplier. Then ker¹(ℚ,G)=1. Use this to remove the residual Hasse obstruction for the locally trivial correction torsor in special-point lifting. Independently, the real-and-abelianized triviality criterion is the existing ET.0 cartesian H¹ theorem.
hypotheses: The target allows arbitrary CM F/F⁺; no imaginary quadratic subfield is assumed.
Derived G is simply connected. The Hasse assertion concerns torsors trivial at every completion.
proofSteps: For the special case F=F⁺E, with E/ℚ imaginary quadratic, use the common-multiplier dual-centre calculation in Shin §3.1. When n and d are odd, the parity relation λ²g^(nd)=1 is exhausted by the centre coboundaries, so the relevant obstruction vanishes.

For arbitrary CM F/F⁺, compute the signed-permutation Galois action on the dual centre and prove that its locally trivial cohomology kernel vanishes. This is the additional group-specific proof obligation; the F=F⁺E calculation by itself does not imply it.
ET.0 duality identifies the resulting dual obstruction with ker¹(ℚ,G). Use ET.0 abelianization for the separately needed real-and-abelianized torsor criterion.
acceptance: Odd dimension and odd totally real degree both enter the parity calculation; they are not dropped.
The arbitrary-CM signed-permutation centre calculation must be supplied; neither an imaginary quadratic subfield nor its simpler action may be silently imposed.

sources.match: Proves the dual-centre calculation in the special case F=F⁺E with E imaginary quadratic, odd d and an odd block; it does not by itself establish the arbitrary-CM assertion.
States the odd-dimensional unitary Hasse assertion for arbitrary CM F/F⁺ of odd totally real degree, and cites Shin’s proof. The extension of that proof is the recorded gap.

nodes.title: Cohomological Mumford–Tate conventions
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A/E, E⊂ℂ a number field, put V_B=H¹_B(A(ℂ),ℚ). Its pure Hodge types are (1,0),(0,1), and V_B⊗ℚ_l≅H¹_et(A_Ē,ℚ_l)≅(T_lA⊗ℚ_l)∨. Let G=MT(V_B) be the whole-Deligne-torus Mumford–Tate group imported from ShimuraData. The smallest ℚ-subgroup containing the complex Hodge cocharacter is the same G: its rationality forces it to contain the conjugate cocharacter and hence the full S-map. A polarization embeds G in GSp(V_B). The inverse Hodge weight is the scalar cocharacter w_s(z)=z·id and ν∘w_s(z)=z².
hypotheses: The standard Hodge action is h(z) acting as z⁻ᵖ z̄⁻ᑫ on V^{p,q}; thus the Hodge weight acts by z⁻¹ on H¹, and w_s is its inverse.
Geometric Frobenius on this cohomological realization has eigenvalues of absolute value √q and multiplier q.
proofSteps: Use the existing Betti/Hodge dictionary, the dual Tate-module comparison and polarizability. Import MT, connectedness and reductivity, without redefining them.
A subgroup over ℚ containing μ contains its complex conjugate; together the two cocharacters recover h_C. This proves equality of the two minimum-group conventions.

Use the alternating polarization with its Tate twist to obtain ν, and evaluate it on scalar matrices to fix νw_s=z². The Hodge Cartan involution supplies an elliptic maximal real torus and compact centre modulo the scalar weight.
acceptance: The negative types (−1,0),(0,−1) belong to homology, not the H¹ used here.

sources.match: Supplies the Mumford–Tate setting; the cohomological Hodge signs are corrected explicitly.
Tensor and polarization descriptions of the Mumford–Tate group; the added Tate multiplier convention must be compared with the subgroup of GL(H¹).

nodes.title: Absolute-Hodge comparison torsor
nodes.statement: For embeddings τ,τ′:E↪ℂ of a number field and an abelian variety A/E, transport the neutral tensor category generated by H¹ and its absolute Hodge tensors from A^τ to A^{τ′}. The scheme P of tensor isomorphisms between the two Betti fibre functors is a torsor under G=MT(A^τ). The comparison identifies MT(A^{τ′}) with the inner form obtained by twisting G by P. Therefore it canonically identifies the two rational conjugacy quotients, independently of a geometric point chosen on P.
hypotheses: All Hodge tensors on these abelian varieties are absolute Hodge, imported from AutomorphicBundles.
Include duals and Tate twists with the cohomological convention; a torsor point is not declared rational.

Fix the transport of the absolute-Hodge tensor category between the two complex embeddings; the quotient identification is independent of the tensor-isomorphism torsor point, relative to that transport.
proofSteps: Use absolute-Hodge transport to build the second fibre functor on the same tensor category. Apply the existing neutral Tannakian tensor-isomorphism torsor theorem.
The two automorphism groups act simply transitively on P, giving the twisting comparison. Changes of a geometric tensor isomorphism are inner, so the conjugacy-quotient comparison is canonical.
Use finite tensor generation to identify the Tannakian automorphism group with the imported MT subgroup, with the Tate multiplier realized as its polarization character.
acceptance: An inner isomorphism exists geometrically; canonicality is asserted only after passing to Conj.

sources.match: Changing the complex embedding gives an inner form via the tensor-isomorphism torsor.

nodes.title: Simultaneous Galois factorization
nodes.statement: For A/E with fixed complex embedding and G=MT(H¹_B(A)), the following condition on E is independent of l: the entire Galois representation ρ_l:Γ_E→GL(H¹_et(A_Ē,ℚ_l)) factors through G(ℚ_l) under Betti–étale comparison. There exists a single finite extension E′/E for which this condition holds for all primes l. Equality of the Galois image closure with G is not asserted.
hypotheses: Use tensor stabilizers and absolute Hodge realizations, not the Mumford–Tate conjecture.
proofSteps: Choose finitely many rational Hodge tensors whose simultaneous scheme-theoretic stabilizer is G. Their absolute-Hodge realizations have algebraic de Rham components, hence are all defined over one finite extension E′.

For σ∈Γ_E, its transform of an absolute Hodge tensor is another such tensor. Equality of their realizations at one l implies equality of the rational tensor, by the comparison isomorphism and faithful scalar extension, and hence equality at every l.
Thus fixing the finite family at one prime is equivalent to fixing it at every prime. Over E′ every tensor is fixed, giving simultaneous factorization.
acceptance: The fixed-field condition concerns all Γ_E, not just its connected algebraic monodromy group.

sources.match: The tensor argument gives l-independent factorization and a common finite extension.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.11, p.19; proof of Theorem 3.8, pp.26–27

nodes.title: Auxiliary groups for good-reduction descent
nodes.statement: Let A/E have good reduction at v|p>2 and all ρ_l factor through G=MT(H¹_B(A)). Construct a totally real F and the common-multiplier H⊂Res_{F/ℚ}G_F, followed by H₁=(H×T)/Z_H, so that the associated Hodge-type datum has a very special parahoric at p, connected-centre compatibility in the sense required by Kisin–Zhou, and a good-reduction point with the same residue field as v. The induced Conj(G)(ℚ̄)→Conj(H₁)(ℚ̄) is injective and Galois equivariant.
hypotheses: The statement uses the exact strongly acceptable Hodge-type triple of Kisin–Zhou §5.1; it does not assert that every Hodge-type integral model has those properties.
The finite field extension used to choose levels must preserve the residue field at v.
proofSteps: Use the p-adic compact image to choose a finite splitting extension over which the chosen Frobenius lift lies in a special parahoric; realize that local extension at all places above p of a totally real F.

Form the common-multiplier fibre product and its Serre-tensor abelian variety. Choose the centralizer torus and central product so its compact central quotient is induced at p. Use the strongly acceptable Hodge embedding and integral-model specialization contract with the same residue field.
Use the diagonal and central-product injection theorems for the quotient comparison, independently of the geometric input.
acceptance: The auxiliary extension does not replace q by q^m: residue-field preservation is necessary to compare the original Frobenius.

sources.match: Constructs the auxiliary common-multiplier and central-product groups and the Hodge-type very-special-parahoric reduction.

nodes.title: Common rational Frobenius class
nodes.statement: Let A/E, G and the fixed complex embedding be as above, assume every ρ_l factors through G(ℚ_l), and let v|p>2 be a place of good reduction with residue field ℱ_q. There is a unique γ_v∈Conj(G)(ℚ) whose realization in Conj(G)(ℚ_l) is χ_G(ρ_l(Fr_v)) for every l≠p, where Fr_v is geometric Frobenius. These elements are semisimple. The class is compatible with changing the complex embedding through the absolute-Hodge quotient isomorphism.
hypotheses: This is a rational point of the affine quotient, not yet a rational element of G.
Use the geometric companion-and-specialization theorem in Kisin–Zhou Theorem 5.1.4, with strongly acceptable Hodge-type triple and good-reduction point.
proofSteps: Apply auxiliary Hodge embedding and the geometric common-class theorem to H₁ at the good-reduction point.

The common H₁ class lies in the geometric image of Conj(G) because one realization comes from G; the injective Galois-equivariant quotient map gives a unique Galois-fixed preimage, hence a rational Conj(G) point.

The geometric theorem itself uses all-representation character comparison to get one common algebraic class, faithful finite-quotient algebraicity, and local-realization descent. Import only that theorem’s precise input, not an unsupported general compatible-system assertion.
Semisimplicity follows from abelian Frobenius semisimplicity. The absolute-Hodge torsor comparison gives embedding compatibility.
acceptance: The characteristic polynomial is monic integral of degree 2 dim A with all complex roots of modulus √q; this alone does not separate classes in G.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2.7 and Remark 6.2.8, p.59; Theorem 5.1.4, pp.47–48
sources.match: The auxiliary group reduces the abelian-variety result to the geometric Frobenius theorem, and quotient injection descends it.

nodes.title: Real representatives in an elliptic torus
nodes.statement: Let G/ℝ be connected reductive, w_s:G_m→Z_G a scalar cocharacter, ν:G→G_m with νw_s(z)=z², and ρ:G↪GL(V) faithful with ρw_s(z)=z·id. Let T⊂G be a maximal real torus with T/w_s(G_m) anisotropic. If a∈Conj(G)(ℂ) has ν(a)=r² for r>0 and every eigenvalue of ρ at its semisimple class has modulus r, then a has a representative t∈T(ℝ).
hypotheses: The condition is on a semisimple representative; an arbitrary nonsemisimple lift is not used.
The quotient torus is anisotropic over ℝ, a stronger pinned weight condition than a bare compact-form assertion.
proofSteps: Choose a semisimple lift in T(ℂ), and divide by w_s(r). All its faithful weights now have modulus one and ν=1. Since the weights generate X*(T), every character value has modulus one.

For a character χ write χw_s(z)=z^m. Complex conjugation c acts by −1 modulo the scalar direction, so χ+cχ=mν: both sides agree on w_s, and their difference is a real-invariant character of an anisotropic torus, hence zero.

For the normalized point t₀, χ(c(t₀))=overline((cχ)(t₀))=overline(ν(t₀)^m/χ(t₀))=χ(t₀). Thus t₀ is real. Multiply back by the specified w_s(r), retaining exactly the original conjugacy quotient point.
acceptance: For G_m, ν=t² and w_s=id, the normalized lift is ±1; restoring r gives ±r, not an arbitrary lift of the trivial central quotient.

sources.match: The intended real elliptic lifting is proved here by a character calculation that supplies semisimplicity and preserves the scalar lift.

nodes.title: Real elliptic Frobenius representative
nodes.statement: The common rational Frobenius class γ_v for A/E has a representative in G(ℝ) contained in an elliptic maximal real torus. Use V_B=H¹ and geometric Frobenius, so ν(γ_v)=q and all eigenvalues have modulus √q.
hypotheses: The Mumford–Tate Hodge/polarization structure supplies an elliptic maximal T with T/w_s(G_m) anisotropic.
proofSteps: Import the Hodge Cartan theorem to choose such a torus. The centre modulo the scalar weight is anisotropic for a polarizable pure H¹ structure.
Apply the weight-normalization theorem with r=√q. The representative belongs to the chosen elliptic torus and has quotient point γ_v exactly.
acceptance: Elliptic means contained in a maximal torus anisotropic modulo Z_G, not that the entire connected centralizer modulo Z_G is compact.

sources.match: States real elliptic lifting; the preceding target repairs the two missing choices in the printed proof.

nodes.title: Rational representatives with one auxiliary place
nodes.statement: Let G/ℚ be connected reductive with simply connected derived group, quasi-split over ℚ_p. Let a∈Conj(G)(ℚ) be a semisimple class with an elliptic representative at infinity and specified semisimple representatives γ_l∈G(ℚ_l) for every l≠p, forming an adelic tuple after choosing a p-component. Then one can choose γ₀∈G(ℚ), elliptic at infinity, which is G(ℚ_l)-conjugate to γ_l for all l≠p except at most one auxiliary prime l₀. The allowable l₀ contain a positive-density Chebotarev set outside any fixed finite set; γ₀ may depend on l₀.
hypotheses: The class is rational and has local representatives at all l≠p; quasi-splitness and the simply connected derived group provide a p-representative and a rational representative in the quasi-split inner form.
An adelic representative tuple and its unramified behaviour are part of the input; arbitrary unrestricted local choices are not automatically adelic.
proofSteps: Choose a rational representative in the quasi-split inner form using ET.0’s semisimple rationality theorem. Form the relative Kottwitz obstruction for the transported adelic tuple, including the chosen real elliptic class.

The real elliptic condition makes the relevant global obstruction group inject into the local obstruction group at an auxiliary prime whose finite Galois action is conjugate to complex conjugation. Chebotarev supplies a positive-density set of such primes.

Duality makes the local modification map surjective onto the global obstruction. Change only the auxiliary local rational class to cancel it, using the local invariant parameterization and simply connected local H¹ vanishing.
Apply the relative form of Kottwitz’s global rationality theorem. The resulting rational representative has all the prescribed classes elsewhere, including the selected real elliptic class.
acceptance: The prime may be chosen from the argument’s positive-density set, not from every externally prescribed positive-density set.

sources.match: Cancels the global obstruction by modifying one auxiliary local class selected by Chebotarev.
The relative-inner-form obstruction criterion produces a global rational element after cancellation.
Applies the argument and notes the positive-density choice of exceptional prime.

nodes.title: Rational Frobenius representative
nodes.statement: In the common Frobenius theorem, assume in addition that G_der is simply connected and G_ℚp is quasi-split. Then γ_v lifts to γ₀∈G(ℚ), elliptic over ℝ, such that γ₀ and ρ_l(Fr_v) are G(ℚ_l)-conjugate for all but at most one prime l≠p. The exceptional prime can be chosen from a positive-density Chebotarev set, and changing it may change γ₀.
hypotheses: Retain p>2 and good reduction; no l=p crystalline assertion is included.
The simply connected and quasi-split hypotheses are not removed.
proofSteps: The common rational quotient class and real elliptic representative provide the global patching inputs.

The compatible cohomological realizations supply the adelic local tuple, with integral unramified behaviour outside finitely many primes through the geometric auxiliary construction. Apply one-prime patching.
acceptance: Geometric conjugacy at all l≠p is stronger than characteristic-polynomial agreement, while rational conjugacy at almost all such primes is a separate refinement.

sources.match: The rational representative conclusion has one possible exceptional prime and the stated extra group hypotheses.
